significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a residual-stream "commit vector" both predicts the earliest point after which an answer remains fixed and causally controls deliberation time when added or ablated; this combines a reasoning-termination phenomenon with a mechanism and reaches form (iii) through a thresholded predictive coupling, rather than merely asserting decodability. It would constrain when later tokens are redundant and explain why two interventions shift stabilization in opposite directions, although its behavioral consequence remains largely bounded to early termination rather than decomposing multiple reasoning failures. A verified-false result would determinately rule out the proposed low-dimensional linear account of commitment, though not nonlinear commitment or ordinary confidence explanations; CALM (Schuster et al., NeurIPS 2022) shows that confidence-triggered adaptive computation already informs consequential accuracy–compute decisions, so establishing whether an internal causal marker supports that decision would matter. In the topic-substitution check, generic "efficient reasoning from a mechanistic perspective" would not justify this score: the extra weight comes specifically from the quoted predictive-and-causal commitment relation.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the "commit-vector projection" combined with a "calibrated threshold" for an early-exit controller, and it is ex ante because it is intended to halt generation "well before the CoT verbally concludes," leaving an action window to save tokens. Its downstream users could include inference-system builders who gate or ship reasoning models, not only interpretability researchers, consistent with the practical uptake demonstrated for confidence-based early exiting by CALM and for self-speculative early exit by LayerSkip (Elhoushi et al., ACL 2024). After per-model re-extraction, the claimed projection-to-stability coupling predicts what should recur, but the submission explicitly allows that "cross-model transfer may fail," so the particular direction and threshold may require rediscovery and calibration rather than transferring intact; the asserted scope nevertheless spans math, logic, code, and model sizes. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: efficient reasoning alone supplies neither this before-the-outcome signal nor its deployment-facing stopping rule.
